selected_goal_name: Fixed Isometric Camera and Projection Setup
selected_goal_description: Replace the disposable perspective test camera with a fixed orthographic isometric camera configuration matching the GDD's Diablo-1/Ultima-Online-inspired fixed 2.5D isometric presentation.
implementation_summary: This was a refine pass on the previously-implemented orthographic isometric camera, correcting two human-Unity-runtime-reported defects without broadening scope. Root cause of "faces wrong direction": BuildCamera() set the camera's rotation (Euler 30,45,0) and its world position offset (10,10,-10) as two independently hand-picked values that did not actually agree - the forward vector produced by that rotation points away from the origin on the X axis rather than back toward it, so the camera's boresight missed the scene. Fix: the camera position is now derived directly from its own rotation (`targetPosition + rotation * new Vector3(0,0,-distance)`), i.e. it is placed by stepping back along its own local -Z axis from the follow target, which mathematically guarantees camera.forward always points exactly at the target regardless of the chosen angle - eliminating the class of bug entirely rather than just re-tuning magic numbers. Distance was kept equal to the original offset's magnitude (sqrt(300)) to preserve the same framing/zoom feel. Root cause of "stationary camera cripples gameplay": the camera had a one-time fixed world position with no tracking of the player. Fix: added a new IsometricCameraFollow component that stores a captured offset (camera position minus target position at Initialize time) and re-applies `target.position + offset` every LateUpdate, translating the camera each frame while never touching its rotation - preserving the fixed isometric orientation and preventing any free/player-controlled rotation, per the evaluator's developer_interpretation. BuildCamera() is now called after BuildPlayer() (minimal reordering) so it can wire the player's transform as the follow target, and the follow component is initialized via an explicit `Initialize()` call (not Awake) to avoid a component-lifecycle ordering pitfall where AddComponent invokes Awake before a caller-assigned target field would be set.
tests_added: Build_MainCamera_ForwardDirectionPointsAtPlayer - asserts the angle between camera.transform.forward and the direction to the player is under 0.5 degrees, directly catching the previous position/rotation mismatch bug

Build_MainCamera_HasFollowComponentTargetingPlayer - asserts an IsometricCameraFollow component exists on Main Camera and its private target field (read via SerializedObject, matching this test file's existing convention) is the Player transform

Build_MainCamera_TranslatesWithPlayerButRotationStaysFixed - moves the player, invokes the follow component's private LateUpdate via reflection (Unity does not run Update/LateUpdate outside Play Mode), and asserts the camera keeps the same relative offset to the player while its rotation is byte-for-byte unchanged

validations.name: Manual math verification of camera-forward-to-target alignment
validations.details: Verified analytically that position = target + rotation*(0,0,-distance) is algebraically equivalent to target - forward*distance (since forward = rotation*(0,0,1) and quaternion rotation distributes over scalar multiples), which guarantees camera.transform.forward points exactly at the target with zero angular error. This directly fixes the reported wrong-direction defect at its root cause.

Confirmed the diff contains exactly the intended camera fix and follow wiring, no stray edits.

Enter Play Mode: confirm the Main Camera view now shows the floor/door/walls centered in frame at the fixed 30/45 isometric angle (not looking off into empty space as before).
Move the player with WASD and confirm the camera translates to keep the player centered/framed, with no visible rotation or tilt change as it follows.
Run Window > General > Test Runner > EditMode and confirm all tests in NoSafeCircle.DoorPrototype.Tests.Editor pass, including the three new camera tests.
Optionally run the existing PlayMode tests (NoSafeCircle.DoorPrototype.Tests) to confirm no regressions from the BuildCamera call-order change (Camera is now built after Player).
requirements_satisfied: Camera remains orthographic (unchanged from the passing part of the prior implementation).

Camera rotation remains the fixed 30/45 dimetric isometric angle and is never modified after scene build, satisfying 'no free player-controlled rotation' and 'consistent isometric viewing orientation'.

Corrected the camera's world position so it is mathematically derived from its own rotation, fixing the reported 'view points in the wrong direction' defect at its root cause rather than re-guessing offset numbers.

Added camera translation/follow behavior (IsometricCameraFollow) so the player/gameplay area stays visible as the player moves, fixing the reported 'stationary camera cripples gameplay' defect, while explicitly not adding any rotation logic.
